results.memo:
PRIORITIES: Play Tropical Island, then cast Birds of Paradise. Next turn play Swamp and cast Grist, the Hunger Tide (3 mana with Birds). Use Grist +1 to mill and make an insect. Then play Forest. After that, Gravebreaker Lamia: search for a Capsule or Seal into the graveyard to stock a lane. Then Muldrotha around the fourth land plus Birds.
THREAT: Edgar Markov (P3) goes wide with vampire tokens, and our wipes are the answer. Giada (P2) grows angels. Watch Sephiroth (P4) for its sacrifice/drain engine.
HOLD: Bojuka Bog: play it as a land drop only when an opponent's graveyard holds real value, or when it's the only land left. Siren Stormtamer: keep it for protecting Grist or Muldrotha from targeted removal. Don't run it out as a 1/1 unless the board is empty.
REPLAN IF: Birds dies (then Grist goes a turn later). P3 floods the board with tokens (then prioritize finding a wipe). Someone plays graveyard hate.

review.biggest_miss: The curve after turn 2 does not add up, and the one protection piece is earmarked for something it cannot protect. Muldrotha costs 6, and the memo says 'fourth land plus Birds', which is 5. Gravebreaker Lamia costs 5 but is slotted onto the 4-mana turn. Siren Stormtamer only protects us or our creatures, and Grist on the battlefield is a planeswalker. The memo also never names the key threat facts: Edgar's eminence makes killing Edgar pointless, and Sephiroth drains off every creature death, including our own wipes.

shortcomings.what: Mana curve is wrong. Muldrotha ({3}{B}{G}{U}) needs 6 sources, not 4 lands plus Birds. Lamia (5 mana) cannot be cast on the Forest turn. Bojuka Bog is 1 of only 4 lands in hand and should be the tapped drop on the turn it costs nothing (turn 3, alongside Stormtamer), not hoarded.
Siren Stormtamer is earmarked to protect Grist. Its ability only counters things that target us or a creature we control, and Grist on the battlefield is a planeswalker, not a creature.

No threat-by-trajectory read. Edgar's eminence makes tokens from the command zone, so killing Edgar does not stop the engine; the answer is wipes. Sephiroth drains on every creature death, so it must die before we wipe.
shortcomings.missing_info: Oracle text of the opponents' commanders (Edgar Markov eminence, Sephiroth's death-drain and transform, Giada's counters) and their likely decklists

shortcomings.what: The Lamia tutor target is generic ('a Capsule or Seal'). The best pick is Claws of Gix, Executioner's Capsule or Sheoldred, depending on board, since that card becomes the first lane cast once Muldrotha lands.
shortcomings.missing_info: Our full decklist (Claws of Gix, Doc Aurlock, Sheoldred, Ratchet Bomb, Massacre Wurm)

shortcomings.what: No win path or clock comparison. Edgar aggro is the fastest clock; we win by locking with recurring wipes/removal and draining later.
Turn order is unknown, so we cannot say who attacks us first or when to hold up instant-speed plays.
shortcomings.missing_info: Seat and turn order (this appears to be our first turn at global turn 4)

errors: Siren Stormtamer cannot protect Grist once Grist is a planeswalker on the battlefield.
'Muldrotha around the fourth land plus Birds' is 5 mana; Muldrotha costs 6.
Gravebreaker Lamia costs {4}{B}, so it is not castable on the turn the Forest makes 4 mana.
review.ideal_memo:
PRIORITIES: T1: Tropical Island, cast Birds. T2: Swamp, Grist (Trop+Swamp+Birds); +1 for an Insect and a mill to stock lanes, and keep the Insect as fodder for Grist -2. T3: Bojuka Bog tapped (exile the best opposing graveyard), cast Stormtamer with spare mana. T4: Forest, Lamia (5 mana); tutor Claws of Gix or Executioner's Capsule to the graveyard, or Sheoldred if boards are wide. Muldrotha needs 6 sources, so prioritize drawn ramp or lands.
THREAT: Edgar (P3) is the fastest clock. Eminence makes vampires from the command zone, so killing Edgar does nothing; plan to wipe (Deluge, Deed, Wurm, Ratchet Bomb). Sephiroth (P4) drains on every creature death, so kill it with Grist -2 before any wipe. Giada (P2) builds big fliers; spot-remove the biggest angel.
HOLD: Stormtamer protects Muldrotha or creatures only, not Grist. Keep U up for it once Muldrotha lands. Don't feed Sephiroth deaths while it lives.
REPLAN IF: Birds dies (Grist on T3, Bog T2). P3 goes wide before T4 (Lamia tutors Massacre Wurm or Toxic Deluge to hand via lanes later). Graveyard hate appears (pivot to hand-cast value).

results.memo:
PRIORITIES: 1) Planetary Annihilation: keep Bayou, Tropical Island, Breeding Pool, Overgrown Tomb, Hinterland Harbor and one Swamp. Sacrifice the other Swamp. 2) Muldrotha is stuck in our graveyard with no recursion in hand, so play for draws. 3) Next turn, cast Gravebreaker Lamia first. Its search puts a card into the graveyard, so pick one we can use from there (a flashback, escape or unearth card, or a reanimation target). If none exists, pick our best reanimation target. 4) Then cast Gray Merchant if mana allows, or hold it (see HOLD).

THREAT: P1's The Scarab God, Teval and zombies from Field of the Dead. P1 is the table's biggest board and should draw everyone's removal.

HOLD: Gray Merchant until our devotion to black is 4+ or P2 is at 4 or less. It is our only reach.

REPLAN IF: We draw reanimation or a wipe. P1 attacks us with 3+ creatures. Our graveyard is exiled. Scarab God targets our graveyard.

review.biggest_miss: The memo reads the board as if Planetary Annihilation had already resolved and missed what it does. It deals 6 damage to every creature. Scarab God, Teval, River Kelpie (it has a -1/-1 counter, so no persist), Hedron Crab, the Zombie and Archangel of Tithes all die. P1 dropping from 13 lands to 6 turns Field of the Dead off. So THREAT and REPLAN (Field zombies, 'P1 attacks with 3+') describe a board that will not exist. The real threat is The Scarab God. It returns to P1's hand at the next end step, and P1 recasts it on the turn after ours. For 4 mana it can then exile our Muldrotha from our graveyard and make P1 a 4/4 Muldrotha. The memo also never names our real outs to rebuy Muldrotha: Animate Dead (2 mana), Demonic Tutor into Animate Dead (4 mana total, fits our 7), Eternal Witness, and Survival into Witness. Instead it has Lamia fetch flashback, escape or unearth cards, which this deck does not run.

shortcomings.what: Did not resolve Planetary Annihilation's 6 damage to each creature. It missed that Scarab God returns to P1's hand, that Field of the Dead turns off at 6 lands, and that the table's creature board is wiped, which leaves our 5/5 lifelink Lamia facing an empty board.

Did not flag that Scarab God can exile Muldrotha from our graveyard and give P1 a copy of our engine. That makes Scarab God the removal priority, ideally exile-based, since it returns to hand when it dies.

Lamia instruction points at flashback, escape or unearth cards the deck doesn't contain. Without Muldrotha on the battlefield, nothing Lamia bins is castable. The fetch should pre-stock a lane (Claws of Gix or Executioner's Capsule) for when Muldrotha returns, and must not bin our outs (Animate Dead, Demonic Tutor, Eternal Witness).
shortcomings.missing_info: Full decklist: no flashback, escape or unearth cards, and exactly which recursion outs exist (Animate Dead, Eternal Witness, Demonic Tutor, Survival of the Fittest).

shortcomings.what: No draw-dependent plan for rebuying Muldrotha. The deck plan explicitly mentions Animate Dead-style auras, and Animate Dead on Muldrotha is a 2-mana line that fits alongside Lamia.

The HOLD condition 'Gray Merchant until devotion 4+' is nearly unreachable. Lamia plus Gary is only 3 devotion, and top-decking another black permanent is unlikely. In a post-wipe top-deck war, a 3-point drain to each opponent plus a body the turn after Lamia beats holding a 5-drop. 'Cast Gary if mana allows' after Lamia is also impossible: 7 mana, two 5-drops cast from hand, and Lamia only discounts graveyard casts.
Turn order was not used. P3 acts before us and P1 after us, so P1's Scarab God recast comes after our turn. That gives exactly one draw step to find a Muldrotha rebuy before our graveyard is at risk.

errors: THREAT lists Scarab God, Teval and Field of the Dead zombies as the on-board threat, but the spell on the stack kills all of them and disables Field at 6 lands.
Implies the Lamia search can make use of flashback, escape or unearth cards, but the deck has none and nothing is castable from the graveyard without Muldrotha.
'Then cast Gray Merchant if mana allows' after Lamia: 7 mana cannot pay for two 5-mana spells from hand, because Lamia's discount applies only to graveyard casts.
review.ideal_memo:
PRIORITIES: 1) Planetary Annihilation: keep Bayou, Tropical Island, Breeding Pool, Overgrown Tomb, Hinterland Harbor and one Swamp; sac the other Swamp. It kills every creature (Scarab God returns to P1's hand at end step) and turns off P1's Field of the Dead. 2) Our turn, 7 mana: if we draw Animate Dead, animate Muldrotha first (2 mana). If we draw Demonic Tutor, fetch Animate Dead and cast both (4 mana). If we draw Eternal Witness, return Muldrotha to hand. 3) Otherwise cast Gravebreaker Lamia and bin Claws of Gix for Muldrotha's return. Never bin Animate Dead, Demonic Tutor or Eternal Witness. 4) Next turn: Gray Merchant (drain 3), then swing Lamia into the empty board at P2 (11).
THREAT: P1's Scarab God, recast after our turn, can exile Muldrotha from our graveyard as P1's 4/4 copy. It is the removal priority; exile it if possible. Teval rebuilds from 7 binned lands. P2 rebuilds on landfall. P3 (33, no board) is last.
HOLD: Any removal we draw is for Scarab God. Gray Merchant waits only for Lamia's devotion.
REPLAN IF: Muldrotha is exiled or stolen. P2 is at 3 or less (Gary lethal). P2 casts another wipe.

results.memo:
PRIORITIES: 1) Cast Muldrotha from the command zone (8 of our 10 mana). 2) Use Muldrotha's land lane: play Misty Rainforest from the graveyard, crack it for an untapped Island or Forest dual. That leaves 3 mana. 3) Cast Grist from the graveyard (planeswalker lane) and +1 for an Insect token. Next turn, -2 sacrificing the Insect to destroy Gitrog. 4) Keep Tropical Island, Darkslick Shores and Mind Stone in hand for later turns.

THREAT: P4's Gitrog Monster. P3's Sauron (7/6) and the Dreadhorde Invasion army. P1's Pantlaza, backed by 5 cards.

HOLD: Shriekmaw for a nonblack Pantlaza or dinosaur. Syr Konrad and Braids until Muldrotha survives a turn cycle.

REPLAN IF: Muldrotha is countered or removed: instead play Tropical Island, cast Mind Stone and Grist. P1 casts Pantlaza. A wrath or graveyard hate appears. Grist is attacked down: use -2 at once.

review.biggest_miss: The memo taps out on Grist, so no {U} is left for Siren Stormtamer. That leaves the just-recast Muldrotha unprotected, reversing the previous memo's explicit 'keep U up' plan. It also misreads the threat picture on three counts. P3's Sauron puts a counter on the deathtouch Army every time we or anyone else casts a spell, making it the fastest-growing threat. P1 is the monarch, and Regal Behemoth doubles their land mana while they hold it. Shriekmaw sits in our graveyard with an open creature lane and a legal nonblack target (Behemoth), yet the memo leaves that lane idle. Finally, the memo has no plan to close on turn 30.

shortcomings.what: It spends all 3 leftover mana on Grist, leaving Stormtamer unable to pay {U} to counter removal on Muldrotha, even though she was apparently just removed again.

It assumes Muldrotha costs 8. The previous memo planned an 8-mana recast last turn and she is back in the command zone, so the tax is probably 4 (cost 10). It also doesn't notice that 6 lands plus Sol Ring make 8 mana, not the reported 10.
shortcomings.missing_info: Number of times Muldrotha has been cast from the command zone and how she left play; a reconciled mana count

shortcomings.what: It misses that Sauron amasses whenever an opponent casts a spell. Our spell-heavy turns feed P3's deathtouch Army, which gets lifelink at 6 power. This makes P3 the fastest trajectory. Sauron's ward (sacrifice a legendary) means edicts are the answer to him.
shortcomings.missing_info: Oracle text for Sauron, Gothmog and Dreadhorde Invasion

shortcomings.what: It misses the monarch. Regal Behemoth made P1 monarch and doubles their land mana. Stormtamer can fly over unopposed to steal it, and attacking doesn't stop it from using its sacrifice ability.
shortcomings.missing_info: Regal Behemoth oracle text / monarch status of the table

shortcomings.what: The creature lane is unused while Shriekmaw sits in the graveyard with a legal target (Regal Behemoth). 'HOLD Shriekmaw' treats a graveyard card as a reactive hand card.

It plays Grist to +1 at 3–4 loyalty into Sauron, Gitrog, Teval and Behemoth, so Grist will likely die before the -2 lands. Vraska Golgari Queen's -3 in the graveyard (MV≤3: Army token, Dreadhorde Invasion, Gothmog) is overlooked.
No win path or clock comparison on turn 30, with every player at 35+ life. Konrad and Braids are held indefinitely with no trigger for deploying them.

errors: 'Grist is attacked down: use -2 at once': loyalty abilities can only be activated at sorcery speed on our own turn.
'HOLD: Shriekmaw': it is in the graveyard and can only be evoked via Muldrotha's creature lane on our turn; it cannot be held reactively. Pantlaza is also not on the battlefield.
Tapping out contradicts Stormtamer's {U} activation cost, so the protection plan doesn't work.
The Muldrotha cost of 8 is likely wrong given repeated recasts (commander tax).
review.ideal_memo:
PRIORITIES: 1) Check Muldrotha's tax (likely 10 now) and cast her first. Every spell we cast adds a counter to P3's Army, so cast only what matters. 2) Land lane: Misty from the graveyard, fetch Underground Sea. Always keep {U} up for Stormtamer. 3) If there are 3+ mana left: evoke Shriekmaw ({1}{B}, creature lane) on Regal Behemoth. Skip Grist; at 3 loyalty it dies before the -2. 4) Attack P1 with Stormtamer to take the monarch (no flyers or reach there). It draws for us and turns off Behemoth. The {U} sacrifice works while tapped. 5) Next turn: Vraska -3 on the Army token or Dreadhorde Invasion, Mulldrifter, then Syr Konrad to start the clock.
THREAT: P3 is fastest. The deathtouch Army grows every upkeep and on every opponent's spell, and gains lifelink at 6 power. Kill it each turn (Vraska, Gwen Stacy, Grist, Ratchet Bomb). Sauron has ward, so remove him with edicts (Braids, Plaguecrafter, Sheoldred). P1: monarch, Behemoth's extra mana, Vortex/Manual cheating dinosaurs, Pantlaza still in the command zone. P4: Gitrog + Teval card and token engine; Grist/Gwen for Gitrog later.
HOLD: {U} for Stormtamer against targeted removal on Muldrotha. Syr Konrad and Braids until Muldrotha has lived one cycle, then Konrad goes down; we must start closing.
REPLAN IF: Muldrotha is countered or wiped: play Tropical Island, cast Mind Stone, evoke Shriekmaw on Behemoth. The Army reaches 5+ power before our turn: it is the first removal target. P1 casts Pantlaza or a 5+ power creature through Vortex. Graveyard hate appears.

results.memo:
PRIORITIES: 1) Play any land drawn first. 2) Cast Talisman of Dominance with Watery Grave and Overgrown Tomb. 3) Cast Seal of Primordium using Zagoth Triome for G. 4) Keep Talisman untapped for Swan Song. 5) Next turn with 4 or more mana, cast Grist first. Use -2 on Sephiroth or Stromkirk Captain, whichever is attacking us. Then cast Braids or Barrin. Then Muldrotha at 6 mana.

THREAT: P4's vampires with Shared Animosity and Edgar still to come. P3's Sephiroth with The Masamune. P2's Atraxa long-term.

HOLD: Hold 1 blue from Talisman for Swan Song, to counter a wipe, Edgar's removal or a key instant. Keep Cryogen Relic until a lethal attack or a draw is needed. Save Seal of Primordium for Masamune, a rock or Shared Animosity. Hold Ratchet Bomb until next turn, then set it at 0 to hit tokens. Glen Elendra waits for 4 or more spare mana.

REPLAN IF: Edgar resolves or P4 reaches 4 or more attackers: cast Grist and Braids for blockers first. Sephiroth equips Masamune and swings at us: Seal the Masamune. We draw Deluge or Deed: prioritize the wipe.

review.biggest_miss: The next-turn plan hinges on 'Grist first, -2 on Sephiroth or Stromkirk Captain', but Grist's -2 needs us to sacrifice a creature and we control none, so that line removes nothing. The memo also misreads who is fastest. P2 has 6 lands, the most mana at the table, and can cast Atraxa next turn. P2 already has Plague Stinger, a flier with infect, and Atraxa's proliferate turns that into a poison clock. Atraxa is answer-on-sight, and the memo files it as 'long-term' and names no answer for it. The answer we hold is Barrin, sacrificing Cryogen Relic (which draws a card on the way out) to bounce Atraxa to the command zone and raise her tax.

shortcomings.what: Plans Grist -2 as immediate removal with no creature on our board to sacrifice. The -2 does nothing. Grist has to +1 first for an Insect, or come down after Braids or Barrin.
shortcomings.missing_info: Full oracle text of Grist, the Hunger Tide: the supplied text was cut off after the +1, and the -2 reads 'You may sacrifice a creature. When you do, destroy target creature or planeswalker.' A strong player would know this anyway.

shortcomings.what: Underrates P2. It has 6 lands against our 3, Atraxa is castable next turn, and Plague Stinger's infect plus proliferate is the fastest plausible kill. No answer is earmarked for Atraxa.

Barrin is not identified as the Atraxa answer. Sacrificing Cryogen Relic to Barrin draws a card and sends Atraxa to the command zone with added tax. That costs 5 mana in one turn, so it also needs a land.
No win path or clock comparison. We are mana-screwed at 3 lands with no land in hand, and Muldrotha at 6 mana is 2+ turns away.

The mana screw is not addressed. Nothing prioritises digging for lands: the Relic sacrifice draws a card, and a land draw lets us cast Barrin and activate it in the same turn. The fetches in our graveyard only become ramp once Muldrotha is out.
Misses that Sephiroth drains us whenever another creature dies, and The Masamune doubles it. That includes our own Grist, Braids and Plaguecrafter sacrifices, so Sephiroth taxes our whole plan.

The Ratchet Bomb at 0 plan hits exactly one opposing token and would kill our own Grist Insects. Edgar's eminence makes tokens from the command zone, so the right targets are the enablers (Shared Animosity, Stromkirk Captain), not tokens.

errors: Grist -2 cannot kill anything without a creature of ours to sacrifice; we control none.
'Play any land drawn first' is stale: we are in main phase 1, the draw has happened, and there is no land in hand.
Ratchet Bomb at 0 would destroy only P4's single Vampire token, plus any Grist Insects of ours.
review.ideal_memo:
PRIORITIES: 1) No land in hand. Cast Talisman of Dominance with Watery Grave and Overgrown Tomb. 2) Cast Seal of Primordium with Zagoth Triome for G, and leave it on board as free instant-speed removal. 3) Pass with Talisman open for Swan Song. 4) Next turn, if Atraxa is out: with 5 mana, cast Barrin and sacrifice Cryogen Relic to bounce her to the command zone (the Relic draws us a card). With 4 mana, cast Grist and +1 for an Insect. Grist's -2 needs a creature to sacrifice. Path: Muldrotha at 6, then recast Plaguecrafter, Seal and fetches every turn, with Braids draining to close.
THREAT: P2 is fastest. It has 6 lands, Atraxa next turn, and Plague Stinger infect plus proliferate is a poison clock. Kill or bounce Atraxa on sight. P4: Captain and Shared Animosity are the multipliers, and Edgar makes a token per vampire cast even from the command zone. P3: Sephiroth drains us for every creature death, ours included, and Masamune doubles it.
HOLD: Talisman U for Swan Song against a wipe or removal. Fire Seal at Shared Animosity at P4's beginning of combat, or at The Masamune once it is equipped. Pay {1}{U} and sacrifice Cryogen Relic to stun a tapped lethal attacker, or to dig for lands. Keep Ratchet Bomb in hand. Glen Elendra waits for 4 spare mana.
REPLAN IF: We draw a land: play it, and Barrin plus an activation fits in one turn. Atraxa resolves: Barrin/Relic bounce, or Grist Insect then -2. P4 reaches 4+ attackers: Seal Animosity and cast Grist for blockers. We draw Deluge or Deed: wipe before Muldrotha.

results.memo:
PRIORITIES: Play Verdant Catacombs now and crack it immediately. Fetch a Swamp-typed blue dual (Watery Grave) if one is in the library, otherwise Overgrown Tomb. We have only two lands, so thin the deck and fix colours. Turn 2: play Wooded Foothills and fetch the missing colour, ideally Breeding Pool, so we have U, B and G. Then cast Cryogen Relic to dig for lands. Turn 3: cast Plaguecrafter or Seal of Primordium, whichever the board needs. Aim for Glen Elendra, Braids and Barrin on turns 4–5.

THREAT: Edgar Markov (P4) goes wide with vampires fastest. Atraxa (P2) is the long-game threat.

HOLD: Seal of Primordium for a real target: Sol Ring or another mana rock, Edgar's anthem, or an Atraxa proliferate engine. Don't spend it on a random rock. Hold Plaguecrafter until a lone creature is worth hitting.

REPLAN IF: We miss land drops (prioritise Cryogen Relic and cheap cantrips). P4 floods tokens early. A turn-1–2 Sol Ring appears (Seal it).

review.biggest_miss: It ignores Sephiroth. That commander drains on every other creature's death and transforms on the fourth death in a turn, so our removal-and-wipe plan feeds it; a wipe into Edgar tokens with Sephiroth alive hands P3 a flipped commander and a big life swing. It also picks a shockland turn 1 when nothing in hand costs 1: Seal and Relic cost 2, and everything else costs more. A tapped Zagoth Triome (all three colours for free) or an original dual is strictly better. It also never mentions Muldrotha: no target turn to cast her, and no plan to protect her.

shortcomings.what: Sephiroth is omitted from the threat read. It punishes our creature removal and wipes (death drains, and it flips on 4 deaths in a turn), so it must be killed before any sweep.

Turn-1 fetch target: it names Watery Grave (2 extra life for untapped mana we can't use). Zagoth Triome (tapped, gives U/B/G) or Underground Sea/Bayou would be better. Pointing at Triome/original duals needs the land list, but 'enter tapped when you have no 1-drop' was reasoning it could have done.
shortcomings.missing_info: Our land list (Zagoth Triome, Underground Sea, Bayou and Tropical Island are all in the deck)

shortcomings.what: No Muldrotha target turn and no plan to protect her. It doesn't say to stock the graveyard (the fetches and Relic give the land and artifact lanes) or to hold Glen Elendra up when she lands. It also doesn't check colour needs: Braids needs BB and Barrin needs UU, which should decide the turn-2 fetch.

No answer earmarking against Edgar's go-wide plan. Spot removal and Plaguecrafter are poor against tokens; the deck's wipes (Toxic Deluge, Pernicious Deed, Ratchet Bomb at 0, Massacre Wurm) are the answer, and Plaguecrafter should be saved for Atraxa or a lone Sephiroth.
shortcomings.missing_info: Which wipes and removal the deck contains

shortcomings.what: No win path or clock comparison at all, even a brief one (a grind into Muldrotha plus Gray Merchant, Vrock or Kokusho drains).
No note that this is a two-land hand, so both fetches are cracked early, leaving nothing in hand to count on for turn 3. Muldrotha can later replay the fetches, so there's no reason to sandbag them.

errors: Choosing Watery Grave untapped on turn 1 pays 2 life for nothing: no card in hand costs 1 (Seal of Primordium and Cryogen Relic both cost 2). And if a Swamp-typed blue dual is wanted, Underground Sea is shock-free and also fetchable with Verdant Catacombs.
review.ideal_memo:
PRIORITIES: T1 play Verdant Catacombs, crack for Zagoth Triome (tapped is free, we have no 1-drop, gives U/B/G); fallback Underground Sea or Bayou, no shock. We're on 2 lands: T2 Wooded Foothills → Bayou (BB for Braids) or Tropical Island (UU for Barrin), untapped, then cast Cryogen Relic to dig. T3 Braids or Barrin; T4 Glen Elendra. Goal: Muldrotha T5–6 with the fetches and Relic already in the graveyard, and Glen mana up to protect her.
THREAT: Edgar (P4) is fastest (a token per vampire cast); answer with wipes (Deluge, Deed, Ratchet at 0, Massacre Wurm), not spot removal. Sephiroth (P3) drains on every death and flips on the 4th death in a turn: kill it BEFORE any wipe. Atraxa (P2) is the slow proliferate engine.
HOLD: Seal for Sol Ring, an Atraxa engine or Edgar's anthem. Plaguecrafter only for Atraxa or a lone Sephiroth, never into tokens. Glen counters for wipes or removal aimed at Muldrotha.
REPLAN IF: No 3rd land by T3 → Relic, hold everything else. Edgar has 4+ tokens by T4 → dig for a wipe, killing Sephiroth first. Early Sol Ring → Seal it.

results.reason: executor escalation: we lost: Professor Dellian Fel; P3: life 30→8 (-22)
results.memo:
PRIORITIES:
1. P3 is at 8 and we have 10 mana. Kill P3 now, in main phase 2.
2. Pay {1} and sacrifice Kokusho to Claws of Gix. Kokusho drains P3 for 5 and Syr Konrad pings for 1, so P3 goes to 2.
3. Pay {1} and sacrifice Baleful Strix to Claws. Konrad pings P3 to 1.
4. Pay {1} and sacrifice Massacre Wurm to Claws. Konrad pings P3 to 0.
5. If a ping fails, recast Kokusho from the graveyard through the creature lane (6 mana) and sacrifice it again.

THREAT: Blood Artist drains us 1 per death. We are at 22, so ignore it. The real risk is P3's one card in hand removing Konrad in response. If that happens, go to the Kokusho recast in step 5.

HOLD: Keep Sheoldred and Muldrotha; never sacrifice them. Keep Konrad until P3 is dead.

REPLAN IF: P3 gains life, Konrad leaves the battlefield, or Claws of Gix is removed.

review.biggest_miss: Blood Artist is the only thing keeping P3 alive, and the memo told the executor to ignore it. Each creature death makes Konrad ping P3 for 1, but Blood Artist gains P3 1 life on the same death, so every sacrifice after Kokusho nets zero. The memo's line actually goes Kokusho (-5-1+1), leaving P3 at 3; then Strix and Wurm do nothing (still 3). It only reaches lethal if the executor happens to read the step-5 fallback broadly, spending all 10 mana. The correct line kills Blood Artist first, which also turns on Massacre Wurm's 2-life loss. Sacrifice Sheoldred to Claws, recast it through the creature lane, and its ETB edict forces P3 to sacrifice Blood Artist, their only creature. That costs P3 a net 3 (Konrad on the graveyard exit, then Wurm 2 plus Konrad 1 minus Artist 1), leaving 5. Then Kokusho's death (5 plus Konrad 1) is lethal, for about 7 mana total.

shortcomings.what: Treated Blood Artist as a harmless drain on us instead of a lifegain source that cancels every Konrad death ping. The lethal math is wrong: P3 ends at 3, not 0.

Never looked for a way to remove Blood Artist first: a Sheoldred recast (edict against a one-creature board) or a Massacre Wurm recast (-2/-2). Either also turns on Wurm's 'loses 2' trigger. Also missed that Konrad fires when a creature card leaves our graveyard during a recast.
Sacrificing Strix and Wurm as 'pings' wastes resources, since they net zero while Blood Artist lives. Sacrificing Wurm also throws away the 2-life-per-creature punisher.
Did not consider Konrad's {1}{B} mill as a finisher. A creature card milled into any graveyard pings P3 with no Blood Artist offset, making it the right leftover-mana sink.
Did not know whether the creature lane was already spent this turn. The previous plan included a Kokusho recast from the graveyard, and every recast line depends on the lane being free.
shortcomings.missing_info: Which Muldrotha lanes (creature/artifact/etc.) have already been used this turn

shortcomings.what: Mana check: only 4 untapped lands plus Signet and Mind Stone are visible, but the state says 10 available. The strategist could not verify which total was right.
shortcomings.missing_info: Accurate breakdown of untapped mana sources

shortcomings.what: Did not know what Sephiroth does, or whether P3 can cast it with 5 open mana to add another death-drain or lifegain effect.
